newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metal futures rise as yen slips.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metal futures rise as yen slips.

text.p: Tokyo precious metal futures ended higher across the board on Wednesday, buoyed by the yen's continued fall against the dollar, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from seven yen to 12 yen per gram higher. Most-active benchmark February was up seven yen at 1,406 yen.
"Considering the yen's steep fall, gold futures did not rise enough, as price gains were offset by massive long-liquidation from private investors," a trader said.
Long-liquidation was countered by trade house buying, while trade houses sold spot gold in arbitrage dealings.
In the spot gold market, bullion was quoted easier at $347.50/348.00 per ounce at 0735 GMT, against $348.30/348.80 in New York on Tuesday.
The dollar rose as far as 126.93 yen in late Tokyo trade, its highest level since August 1992.
Japanese traders said the upside for gold and platinum futures was likely to be capped by long-liquidation amid caution that prices were already at high levels.
In nervous trading, palladium futures extended early gains to end higher, backed by the yen's further dip against the dollar late in the day, the traders said.

"Private investors still hold massive shorts in TOCOM palladium futures, while buying interest from overseas funds remains strong on the continued delay in Russian exports to Japan," one trader said. "If the yen continues to slip, private investors will be forced to cover their shorts," he said.
Short-term palladium lease rates jumped during Asian hours.

Short-covering by dealers and a lack of lenders were the main reasons behind the higher lease rates. Benchmark February palladium added 10 yen per gram at 589 yen. Benchmark February platinum was up eight yen per gram at 1,468 yen. Benchmark February silver was up 0.3 yen per 10 grams at 196.4 yen.
